prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1115; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant reporting a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection, with the claimant's vehicle stopped at the light when struck from behind.

Entry 2: Confirmed the claimant is a listed driver on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss; nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses place the claimant inside the vehicle and describe the impact in the same way the claimant did; the other driver has also confirmed the sequence of events.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show rear bumper and trunk damage consistent with the reported impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 5: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash from a crash of this type; no prior injury to the neck or upper back appears in the claimant's records.

Entry 6: Claimant followed the recommended treatment plan, with physiotherapy and follow-up visits; the provider notes show steady improvement and the treatment frequency reduced as symptoms eased.

Entry 7: In a follow-up call the claimant added a few minor details about the traffic conditions and the moment of impact, but the core account has not changed from the original statement.

Entry 8: Reviewed the file with the injury course, the vehicle damage and the witness accounts all in line; the claim is consistent with the reported loss and is progressing toward settlement review.
